key_insight: Graph neural networks are now the go-to model for relational data, but their value depends on whether graph structure truly adds signal beyond the extra compute.
clinical_relevance: For healthcare and clinical NLP, GNNs may help when patient, document, or biomedical relationships are explicit, but gains should be checked against simple baselines and real deployment constraints.
method: Frames GNNs through one unified design space covering spectral and spatial formulations.
Links model expressiveness to the Weisfeiler-Leman hierarchy to clarify what architectures can and cannot distinguish.
Compares performance across 12 domains and separates genuine gains from weak-baseline or split-related artefacts.
evidence_signal: The survey synthesizes evidence across twelve domains and emphasizes that evaluation quality matters, noting that reported gains can be inflated by favourable splits or weak baselines.
watch_item: Temporal graphs, heterophily, scaling limits, and deployment issues such as robustness, fairness, and explainability remain major barriers.
paper_title: Graph Neural Networks Applications Across Domains: All Insights You Need
